messages:
maya_ops: FYI customer acme-corp (Private deployment in eu-west-1) reports intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures to our private control plane starting ~14:23 UTC. Happening across 3 app instances. They say it spikes right after a VPN rekey.

maya_ops: attached snippets from their vpn logs and a short traceroute. Looks like DNS is flipping between a hostname and an IP and some packets are being blackholed.

maya_ops: logs:
```
14:23:12 IKEv2: rekey negotiated, child SA lifetimes 3600s
14:23:14 ESP: recv invalid spi 0x0 from 54.23.12.7
14:23:17 TLS: handshake failed: timeout
14:23:18 kernel: XFRM: state add failed: -22
```

maya_ops: traceroute (partial):
```
1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.3 ms
2  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  1.2 ms
3  54.23.12.7 (54.23.12.7)  12.8 ms  <-- peer esp gateway
4  * * *
```

maya_ops: note: customer says their onprem firewall does NAT over the VPN and they have a DNS stub resolver that alternates between resolving control plane hostname to private peering IP and public IP. Could be sending traffic down wrong path after rekey.

samir_net: Do we know if NAT-T (UDP/4500) is allowed both directions? If NAT-T blocked you can get ESP-only which fails across most NATs. Also need to confirm IKE lifetimes match on both sides. Ask customer for pcap around rekey and ip xfrm state.

samir_net: Example checks to run on customer box: 
```
# show ip xfrm state
# sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc
# tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 54.23.12.7 and port 500 or port 4500 -w rekey.pcap
```

alex_m: Also ask them to check for PMTU/DF issues. If MTU drops during rekey they might fragment ESP which some firewalls drop. On AWS DX/VIF the MTU and BGP path can cause blackholing. Ask them to check if DF is set and whether iptables/clamp MSS is used.

alex_m: Relevant sysctl we saw in past issues: 
```
net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc = 0  # enable PMTU discovery
# recommended MSS clamp on iptables: --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

rao_support: Opening a ticket with the customer to collect pcap and config. Asked them to confirm firewall rules allow UDP 500/4500, ESP (protocol 50) and that their DNS stub resolver is not flipping to public IPs for control plane during failover. Also asked them to check BGP advertised prefixes on DX side for accidental overlap.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-789 and paging oncall-sre.

maya_ops: Customer sent pcap and shows IKE rekey followed by immediate ESP recv invalid spi and then client connections to control-plane endpoint that resolve to the private-peering IP but are routed over public internet due to a stale route on their directconnect router. pcap snippet showing NAT-T present but some ESP packets never complete handshake.

maya_ops: pcap excerpt: 
```
14:23:12.001 IKE_SA_INIT(ikev2) from 10.10.0.5:500 -> 54.23.12.7:500
14:23:14.221 UDP 4500 from 10.10.0.5:4500 -> 54.23.12.7:4500 (NAT-T)
14:23:14.500 ESP (encrypted) SPI 0xdeadbeef
14:23:14.502 ESP (encrypted) SPI 0x0  <-- invalid, gets dropped
```

samir_net: That invalid SPI on ESP after rekey can be seen when one side deleted old SA too early or there's asymmetric routing. If the DX router has a stale next-hop for the private prefix it will push ESP out the wrong interface. Also if the customer's firewall rewrites source IP (masquerade) inconsistently across rekeys the peer will reject the SA.

alex_m: Quick repro steps we used on staging to replicate: create a NAT that toggles source IP across rekey, force IKE rekey, watch ESP invalid spi and TLS handshake fail. We fixed by aligning rekey timers (set child SA to 1h both sides), enabling NAT keepalive, and ensuring UDP/4500 allowed. Also applied MTU clamp 1400 on the peer facing interface and enabled --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on NAT.

rao_support: Customer applied temporary firewall change to allow UDP 4500 both ways and removed a stale static route on their DX router that was pointing the private peering prefix at the internet egress. They also set MSS clamp and lowered MTU to 1400.

rao_support: Monitoring shows control plane TLS errors dropped to zero and API 502 rate returned to baseline within 6 minutes of the changes. Customer confirmed stability across the 3 app instances.

maya_ops: Action items captured: 
- customer to keep UDP 4500/500 and ESP allowed in firewall rules
- align IKE/child SA lifetimes (we suggested 3600s/3600s as baseline)
- enable NAT keepalive on customer's firewall for persistent NAT translation
- clamp MTU / MSS on DX-facing router to 1400 if using NAT over VPN
- fix DNS stub resolver to prefer VPC-private A record for control-plane while in peering state

rao_support: Closing the support escalation, will follow-up with a short postmortem template and config recommendations to include in onboarding docs.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-789 marked resolved by rao_support
